newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger rules out by-election for NZ First seat.
newsitem.headline: Bolger rules out by-election for NZ First seat.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Wednesday virtually ruled out a by-election in Te Tai Hauauru, the seat held by New Zealand First MP, Tukoroirangi Morgan.
Speculation has been mounting that Morgan might be forced to resign following the disclosure that he used Aotearoa TV money to buy expensive clothes for himself.
The government this week pulled the plug on the Maori TV station citing serious reservations about financial management and controls.
After his state of the nation address to the Auckland Chamber of Commerce today, Bolger said no work had been done on a by-election if New Zealand First was forced to vacate the seat.
"Can I say as leader of the National Party and leader of the Government, no work is going on. We simply do not expect one," he told the New Zealand Press Association.
"It is not something we are in any way, shape or form addressing. We don't expect anything like that to happen. There may have been some mistakes made but that's that."
On Tuesday the Government said it was exploring the law and what would happen if a by-election was forced by the row.
Bolger said he was not distancing himself from something Morgan did before he became an MP.
"He was a journalist, he wasn't a Member of Parliament."

Morgan was a NZ First candidate when he, fellow director Morehu McDonald and an unnamed presenter spent $16,000 of Aotearoa TV's money on clothes for themselves, including an $89 pair of underpants for Morgan.
Bolger said it was a concern that Aotearoa Television was not particularly well managed and it was not an appropriate vehicle to go further with public funds.
